items.decisionPrompt: An adult wants exercise-related body-mass reduction. Which nutritional strategy is more likely to matter over time?
items.optionA: Change meal timing while keeping total energy intake above expenditure.
items.optionB: Maintain an appropriate, sustained energy deficit.

evidenceSources.citation: Jensen MD, et al. 2013 AHA/ACC/TOS guideline for the management of overweight and obesity in adults. Circulation. 2014;129(25 Suppl 2):S102-S138. doi:10.1161/01.cir.0000437739.71477.ee.

items.decisionPrompt: An endurance athlete can tolerate food before a prolonged morning performance session. Which preparation is preferable?
items.optionA: Begin the session after an overnight fast.
items.targetPopulation: Healthy endurance athletes preparing for a prolonged aerobic performance session

evidenceSources.citation: Aird TP, Davies RW, Carson BP. Effects of fasted vs fed-state exercise on performance and post-exercise metabolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. 2018;28(5):1476-1493. doi:10.1111/sms.13054.

items.decisionPrompt: A healthy athlete with an adequate diet begins a new endurance-training block. Which antioxidant strategy is preferable?
items.optionA: Rely on dietary sources unless a specific deficiency or indication is identified.
items.optionB: Add a high-dose antioxidant supplement immediately after training.

evidenceSources.citation: Pastor R, Tur JA. Antioxidant Supplementation and Adaptive Response to Training: A Systematic Review. Current Pharmaceutical Design. 2019;25(16):1889-1912. doi:10.2174/1381612825666190701164923.

items.decisionPrompt: An endurance athlete finishes a glycogen-depleting session and must train again in less than four hours. Which recovery plan is preferable?
items.optionA: Begin carbohydrate-focused refueling promptly after the first session.
items.optionB: Wait until the regular evening meal to begin carbohydrate refueling.
items.targetPopulation: Healthy endurance athletes with less than four hours between demanding sessions

items.decisionPrompt: Is creatine monohydrate generally evidence-supported for healthy adults pursuing strength?
items.optionA: Consider it evidence-supported when no contraindication applies.

evidenceSources.citation: Kreider RB, et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation in exercise, sport, and medicine. Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition. 2017;14:18. doi:10.1186/s12970-017-0173-z.

items.decisionPrompt: An endurance athlete prioritizes performance in an event lasting more than 90 minutes and tolerates carbohydrate during exercise. Which fueling plan is preferable?
items.optionB: Use water without carbohydrate during the event.

items.optionB: Treat adequate daily protein as relevant.
